title: Free cocompletion by space-valued presheaves
statement:
Use the infinity categories and nested universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U\prime$ of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], and the coherent functor and mapping-space conventions of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Small means $\mathcal U$-small, and $\mathcal S$ denotes the infinity category of small spaces. Let $D$ be a small infinity category. The infinity category $\mathcal P(D)=\operatorname{Fun}(D^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)$ has small mapping spaces and admits all small colimits. Write $j:D\to\mathcal P(D)$ for $d\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_D(-,d)$. For every infinity category $\mathcal V$ in the larger universe admitting all small colimits, restriction along $j$ induces an equivalence of infinity categories
$$j^*:\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{colim}}(\mathcal P(D),\mathcal V)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(D,\mathcal V),$$
where the left side is the full subcategory of coherent functors preserving small colimits. The equivalence includes natural transformations and their higher simplices, so an equivalence between the restrictions of two such functors lifts to a natural equivalence between those functors.

source.place: Corollary 5.1.2.4 and Theorem 5.1.5.6, printed pp. 318 and 327; the usual small-mapping-space convention for presheaves on a small infinity category Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks Project tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: For $F,G\in\mathcal P(D)$, [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] supplies $\mathcal U$-small right fibrations $E_F,E_G\to D$ and identifies their over-map Kan complex with $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P(D)}(F,G)$. Its $n$-simplices are maps $E_F\times\Delta^n\to E_G$ over $D$. These form a small set in each degree, and the countable collection of degrees is small. Thus the mapping space has a small model. The same argument in $\mathcal U'$ proves local $\mathcal U'$-smallness of $\widehat{\mathcal P}(D):=\operatorname{Fun}(D^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S_{\mathcal U'})$, formed in one further containing universe.

source.place: Section 3.3.2; size of the right-fibration mapping model.

proof.text: Fix a small simplicial set $K$. Small colimits exist in $\mathcal S$ by [lem-coef-spaces-small-colimits-universe]. By the dual cone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], each colimit cocone is a universal arrow $p\to\Delta_K L$. The opposite assertion of [lem-coef-parametric-universal-arrows], applied to $\Delta_K:\mathcal S\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal S)$, assembles them into a coherent left adjoint $\operatorname{colim}_K$ and gives its mapping-space adjunction also on $D^{\mathrm{op}}$-diagrams. The simplicial exponential identity curries those diagrams as $K$-diagrams in $\mathcal P(D)$. Under this identity the adjunction is precisely between objectwise $\operatorname{colim}_K$ and the constant $K$-diagram functor on $\mathcal P(D)$. Its unit is a colimit cocone by the same cone criterion. This constructs all small colimits in $\mathcal P(D)$, including $K=\varnothing$. The objectwise criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] identifies their evaluations. Apply the same argument in $\mathcal U'$ for the larger presheaf category.

source.place: Corollaries 5.1.2.3-4, printed p. 319; coherent pointwise adjunction argument.

proof.text: Let $\iota:\mathcal P(D)\to\widehat{\mathcal P}(D)$ be objectwise universe inclusion. Its values preserve small colimit cocones by [lem-coef-spaces-small-colimits-universe]; objectwise detection from [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] therefore proves that $\iota$ does too. Write $j'$ for the Yoneda functor into $\widehat{\mathcal P}(D)$. The construction of [def-coef-infinity-presheaf-yoneda] gives $\iota j=j'$ up to the canonical identification: its rigidification of $D$, the Kan complexes $\operatorname{Sing}|\mathfrak C[D](d,e)|$, and their precomposition and postcomposition maps are unchanged on enlarging the universe. The space model in [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces] likewise retains these very Kan complexes and maps. This identifies the coherent functors, not just their values.

source.place: Corollary 5.1.2.3; Section 5.1.3; universe-independent explicit Yoneda construction.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], $j$ is fully faithful, $D$ having small mapping spaces; Yoneda evaluation [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-evaluation] gives $\operatorname{Map}(j(d),F)\simeq F(d)$. Let $A$ be its full essential image; [lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image] supplies an equivalence $J:D\simeq A$, a quasi-inverse $k$, and a counit $Jk\simeq1_A$. By [lem-coef-infinity-presheaf-representable-slice-density], for every $F$ the actual canonical cocone $\delta_F:(A_{/F})^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal P(D)$ is colimiting, and $A_{/F}$ is essentially small. Put $a_F:A_{/F}\to A$ for its source projection. Choose a small quasicategory $T_F$ and an equivalence $r_F:T_F\simeq A_{/F}$. These choices are used to test colimits; the extension functor below will be supplied coherently by relative Kan existence.

source.place: Lemma 5.1.5.3 and Lemma 5.1.5.5; replete-image version uses essential smallness.

proof.text: For any quasicategory $\mathcal E$, the functor $p:\mathcal E\to *$ is an isofibration: inner horns lift by the quasicategory axiom, and identities lift the sole equivalence of $*$. For a join cocone with boundary $b:K\to\mathcal E$ and apex $x$, [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-constant-test] says that being a $p$-colimit is equivalent to the homotopy-pullback condition with upper map $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,z)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)}(b,\Delta_Kz)$ for every $z$. Both lower spaces are points. Thus that condition is exactly that the upper map be an equivalence, which is the ordinary colimit criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. The opposite join comparison of [lem-coef-infinity-join-cone-calculus] converts coherent cocones with fixed boundary to join cocones. Hence, with that conversion, ordinary colimits and $p$-colimits coincide. All these statements may be used in a containing universe when $K$ is essentially small.

source.place: Section 4.2 and Lemma 4.3.2.13: verification of the relative-colimit hypothesis for the map to a point.

proof.text:
Fix $f:D\to\mathcal V$ and put $f_A=fk$. For each $F$, small cocompleteness of $\mathcal V$ gives a colimit of $f_Aa_Fr_F$. Step 5 converts it into a join $p$-colimit with exactly this boundary, for $p:\mathcal V\to *$. Clause (2) of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence] transports existence of that local lift along $r_F$ to a $p$-colimit on $A_{/F}$ with boundary exactly $f_Aa_F$. Its hypothesis that $p$ is an inner fibration holds by step 5. Enlarge the containing universe for these slices without changing the smallness needed to form the original colimits. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-relative-kan-existence] to $A\subseteq\mathcal P(D)$, $h=f_A$, and the unique base functor to $*$. The equality on the base is automatic, and the required local lifts are the ones just obtained. It supplies a coherent $H:\mathcal P(D)\to\mathcal V$, restricting exactly to $f_A$, for which every $H\delta_F$ is a $p$-colimit. Step 5 and reindexing by clause (2) give
$$H(F)\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{t\in T_F}f_A(a_Fr_F(t)).$$
The unit $kJ\simeq1_D$ gives $Hj\simeq f$. Only the testing presentations $T_F$ were chosen separately; coherence of $H$ comes from the cited existence theorem.

source.place: Lemma 5.1.5.5(2), using Lemma 4.3.2.13 and exact-boundary equivalence of local cone lifts.

proof.text:
Fix $v\in\mathcal V$ and work in $\mathcal U'\in\mathcal U''$; $\mathcal V$ and $\widehat{\mathcal P}(D)$ are locally $\mathcal U'$-small (step 1). The coherent mapping bifunctors of [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] give $Q_v=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(f(-),v)$ on $D^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $G_1=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(H(-),v)$, $G_2=\operatorname{Map}_{\widehat{\mathcal P}(D)}(\iota(-),Q_v)$ on $\mathcal P(D)^{\mathrm{op}}$, valued in $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U'}$. Whiskering by $Jk\simeq1_A$ ([lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image]), $\iota j=j'$ (step 3) and Yoneda evaluation [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-evaluation] in $\mathcal U'$ give $G_2|_{A^{\mathrm{op}}}\simeq Q_vk^{\mathrm{op}}=G_1|_{A^{\mathrm{op}}}$, the equality as $H|_A=fk$. Step 5 and clause (2) of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence] make $\delta_Fr_F^{\triangleright}$ a small colimit; step 3 and clause (2) then make $\iota\delta_F$ a colimit. By [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] contravariant representables send $\iota\delta_F$ and $H\delta_F$ (step 6) to limits, so $G_1,G_2$ carry $\delta_F^{\mathrm{op}}$ to limit cones. Clause (4) identifies $\delta_F^{\mathrm{op}}$ with the canonical cone on $(A^{\mathrm{op}})_{F/}$. Thus [lem-coef-infinity-kan-mapping-restriction], second hypothesis for $G_2$, lifts the equivalence on $A^{\mathrm{op}}$ to $\theta:G_1\to G_2$. Each $\theta_F$ maps the limit cone $G_1\delta_F^{\mathrm{op}}$ to $G_2\delta_F^{\mathrm{op}}$ by equivalences on the diagram; the limit criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], natural in diagrams, makes $\theta_F\circ-$ an equivalence on all mapping spaces, so $\theta_F$ is one. By [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] $\theta$ is a natural equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(H(F),v)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\widehat{\mathcal P}(D)}(\iota F,Q_v).$$

source.place: Lemma 5.1.5.5(1): mapping-presheaf proof of preservation, with larger-valued spaces for an arbitrary target; naturality via restriction of transformations along the canonical slice (Lemma 4.3.2.12).

proof.text:
Prove that $H$ preserves every small colimit. Let $p:K\to\mathcal P(D)$ have colimit cocone with apex $L$, with $K$ any $\mathcal U$-small simplicial set. Step 3 says that $\iota L$ with the image cocone is the colimit of $\iota p$. Testing against $v\in\mathcal V$, step 7 and the mapping-space colimit criterion give
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(H(L),v)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\widehat{\mathcal P}(D)}(\iota L,Q_v)\simeq\lim_{k\in K^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\widehat{\mathcal P}(D)}(\iota p(k),Q_v)\simeq\lim_{k\in K^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(H(p(k)),v).$$
Naturality from step 7 identifies this composite with precomposition by the cocone $Hp\to\Delta H(L)$. The same colimit criterion proves that this cocone is colimiting. Thus $H$ preserves small colimits, including the empty colimit; $K=\varnothing$ makes both limiting mapping spaces terminal. This proves essential surjectivity of the stated restriction functor for every permitted $\mathcal V$.

source.place: Lemma 5.1.5.5(1), expressed through the larger-space mapping presheaf; Theorem 5.1.5.6

proof.text:
Let $B_1,B_2:\mathcal P(D)\to\mathcal V$ preserve small colimits. Reindex the canonical cocone of step 4 along $r_F:T_F\simeq A_{/F}$: this is a small colimit, so $B_1$ preserves it. Clause (2) of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence] and step 5 then show that $B_1\delta_F$ itself is colimiting for every $F$. The first hypothesis of [lem-coef-infinity-kan-mapping-restriction] is therefore satisfied for $A\subseteq\mathcal P(D)$, $F=B_1$, $G=B_2$. It gives an equivalence on the mapping spaces between these functors and their restrictions to $A$. Restriction along $D\simeq A$ is also an equivalence on functor categories: precomposition with a quasi-inverse is its inverse, with the natural equivalences obtained by whiskering those of $D\simeq A$. Hence restriction along $j$ induces an equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}(B_1,B_2)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(B_1j,B_2j).$$
This is the actual restriction map, coherent under precomposition and postcomposition by the cited statement. Thus $j^*$ is fully faithful on the full subcategory of colimit-preserving functors.

source.place: Lemma 4.3.2.12 and Corollary 4.3.2.16; colimit-preserving direction of Lemma 5.1.5.5(1)

proof.text: The source full subcategory and both functor categories are quasicategories in a sufficiently large auxiliary universe by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Steps 6-8 show that every target object $f$ is equivalent to $Hj$, and step 9 shows that $j^*$ is fully faithful. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image] to $j^*$; its full essential image is all of $\operatorname{Fun}(D,\mathcal V)$, so it has a coherent quasi-inverse. This is the claimed equivalence of infinity categories, retaining transformation spaces and their higher compositions. In particular an equivalence between two restrictions lifts to an equivalence upstairs: apply the quasi-inverse to that edge and compose with the quasi-inverse unit equivalences.
